units.text: INT. LAKE CABIN, KITCHEN - DAY
A pine-panelled kitchen that smells of woodsmoke and dust.
Cardboard boxes stack on a table where somebody's father once ate breakfast.
Through the window a grey lake lies flat as a plate.
MARGUERITE LAVOIE, fifty-two, in a cardigan, wraps a chipped teacup in newspaper.
Her sister ODILE LAVOIE, forty-eight, in a denim jacket, stands at the open refrigerator with a bin bag, holding a jar of pickles at arm's length.
At the counter DESMOND OYELARAN, Marguerite's husband, taps at a calculator.
By the screen door a neighbour, MR. ALBRECHT, seventy, in rubber boots, holds a fishing rod he has not been asked to hold.
That was Maman's cup.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: It's chipped.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: It was chipped when she bought it.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: She sets the cup in the box.
She does not look at her sister.
She picks up the next cup.
He kept pickles from 2009.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: He kept everything.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: That's not a virtue.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: She drops the jar in the bin bag.
The glass thuds, muffled, and does not break.
Both of them listen for it to break.
Neither says so.
The realtor wants to list by the fifteenth.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: The fifteenth is a Sunday.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: Then the sixteenth.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: She'll list when she's ready.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: Who's she?
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: You. She. I don't know.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: She ties the bag.
She carries it past Mr. Albrecht, who steps aside, then follows with the rod.
Your father lent me this in '94.
units.name: MR. ALBRECHT

units.text: Keep it.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: It isn't mine to keep.
units.name: MR. ALBRECHT

units.text: He'd want you to have it.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: She sets the bag at the curb.
The screen door bangs behind her.
Marguerite stands very still at the table, her hand flat on a cardboard lid.
Marguerite.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: I'm fine.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: I know.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: He crosses the kitchen and unfolds her fingers from the lid.
He takes the cup out of the box, unwraps it, fills it from the kettle, and puts it in her hands.
I'll leave the rod on the porch, then.
units.name: MR. ALBRECHT

units.text: He goes.
The kitchen is quiet.
Through the window Odile has sat down on the dock, her back to the cabin, her boots dangling above the water.
Marguerite watches her through the glass.
She lifts the cup, drinks, and does not set it down.
After a moment she carries the cup out the screen door and across the grass.
She lowers herself onto the planks beside her sister.
She holds the cup out without a word.
Odile takes it.
She drinks.
She hands it back.
The lake does not move.
